proposed_fixes.title: Verify self-contained runtime deployment across installation paths
plan: Reproduce clean install and the reported upgrade sequences separately for the trusted official installer and affected third-party packaging, retaining each distribution identity.
Compare the generated runtime manifest, root source files and final WinUI runtime copies; correlate installer custom-action results and actual apphost resolution before applying any workaround.

Correct only the demonstrated incomplete deployment path and add or extend post-install/update smoke checks for Settings and other affected self-contained applications. Preserve regular-copy isolation and idempotent repair; coordinate distribution-specific changes with its existing maintainer.

confidence.rationale: The participant trace and runtime-layout workaround support a dependency-deployment class, while exact-release code already implements copying and multiple installation methods remain unresolved.

verification: Trusted clean install, in-place update and repair start Settings and relevant WinUI applications without requiring an unrelated shared runtime installation.
Every applicable runtime-manifest entry has a valid deployed source and usable destination with correct architecture/version.
Verify Explorer preview and low-integrity loads still work; do not reintroduce shared-inode ACL coupling by replacing regular copies with blanket hardlinks.
proposed_fixes.root_cause: The supplied Settings host trace cannot resolve its self-contained hostpolicy dependency. Missing/incomplete runtime copying is supported for that installation; skipped custom actions, update leftovers, payload omission and other package-specific paths are not yet distinguished.

judgment.recommended_action: Run a distribution-specific clean/update deployment matrix and verify the installed runtime closure; do not recommend unreviewed hardlink scripts or mixing runtime files.
evidence: The full thread includes Scoop, Chocolatey, manual-installer and WinGet participants; reinstalling succeeds for some but not all.
ScoopInstaller/Extras18020 is merged and specifically copies required runtime files for that distribution. It does not prove every later participant is fixed.

A supplied Settings apphost trace treats the app as self-contained, then fails to locate hostpolicy.dll in the resolved runtime directory. Installed shared Desktop Runtime versions alone do not repair that deployment state.
Participants report a manual runtime-file hardlink workaround, but results vary and the latest discussion still reports failures.

Exact0.102.3001 installer source already deduplicates matching WinUI runtime files and recreates regular copies through the historically named CreateWinAppSDKHardlinksCA. It explicitly avoids shared-inode hardlinks because of Explorer preview/DACL consequences.
judgment.rationale: The thread is not universally resolved by the Scoop PR or by installing another Desktop Runtime version. The provided trace establishes a dependency-layout failure for that participant, not one universal cause for every runtime prompt. Current installer code already contains a copy path and trailing-separator normalization, so proposing those changes again would ignore counterevidence. Reproduce the actual distribution/update sequence and verify manifest entries, source payload and completed copy operation before correcting a remaining path. Unfixed, affected self-contained applications cannot launch.
